_note: v4: after audit loops 1 (art direction) and 2 (buildability). Reference image 1 = real-time render of the actual 3D car model (front three-quarter). Reference image 2 = the same model from the side. Commercial frames use photo panels because no good open-source van model exists; in the build those panels hold EveryWrap's real job photos. v4 (loop 3, prompt mechanics only): each frame is restructured as format line, scene, car (with explicit nose/tail sides), a numbered list of the exact on-screen strings, palette; shared_tail holds the global negatives. Glyphs: the ellipsis character became three periods, the '‹ ›' stepper arrows are described as chevron icons, and the '|' in the switch is replaced by a described two-segment toggle. Commercial frames state that the reference car does not appear.
shared_tail: OUTPUT RULES: show only the web page itself as one flat, full-bleed screenshot filling the whole canvas: no browser window, address bar or tabs; no laptop, monitor or phone frame; no phone status bar. Render only the text listed above, each item once, spelled exactly as given, crisp and legible, light text only on dark areas and dark text only on light areas; no other words, numbers, captions, labels, page titles, logos or watermarks. No people, no hands, no robot, mascot or avatar. IF THE SPORTS CAR APPEARS: it is exactly the car in the reference images (same body shape, proportions, wheels and details) but with no badges or logos anywhere, no licence plate, and plain black tyre sidewalls with no lettering or coloured marks; it looks like a high-end real-time 3D render (WebGL), clean and crisp, not a photograph. Nothing from the references other than the car itself is copied.

concepts.name: One Light
concepts.idea: Quiet luxury. A black wrap booth, one long light, and a seam of vinyl that travels over the car: moving to the next service pulls a new seam across it.
concepts.signature: The seam is the transition. Scrolling or stepping to the next service drags a glowing seam nose to tail and the car comes out the other side changed (wrapped, glossier under protection film, glass darkened, carbon trim added), with a slow camera orbit.

concepts.name: Finish Library
concepts.idea: A bright material lab. The finish name is the set: giant letters stand behind the car, and the finishes are physical vinyl sample cards you pick up.
concepts.signature: Pick a vinyl sample card (drag it onto the car on desktop, tap it on a phone) and the car re-wraps while the giant word behind it changes to the new finish name.

concepts.name: Light Tunnel
concepts.idea: Motion. The car sits in a tunnel of moving light arches, the way finishes are shown in car films: reflections race over the bodywork and every finish reads instantly.
concepts.signature: Light arches stream past the car and each service changes how they behave: Wrap is a burst of speed, PPF one slow bright sweep, Tint dims the arches while the glass goes dark, Kits drops the camera low. Pointer or phone tilt steers the light.
